operations.summary: Project filesystem growth from observed storage gauges
operations.description:
Read-only, tenant-scoped projection of node_disk_used_bytes with
contemporaneous node_disk_total_bytes or used plus free bytes. The
latter is effective usable capacity, not physical disk capacity.
Uses a 14-day window with hourly query evaluation, retaining actual
source observation times and deduplicating repeated lookback values.
Counts describe hourly sampled observations, not all ingested samples;
sparse observations outside the backend lookback may be absent. No
interpolation or per-service storage attribution is performed. Separate
origin/source streams remain separate resources and are never summed.
Guard OTLP times describe Guard collection, not original OTLP point time.
Unknown capacity, stale/inadequate history and inconsistent measurements
return an explicit state without an exhaustion estimate. Exhaustion is
a growth scenario range measured from the latest observation, not a
statistical confidence interval. Both bounded queries share a timeout.

operations.summary: Queue an owned server OS update plan, OS update or reboot
operations.description: Requires the Edge-signed `techstack.servers.maintenance` entitlement, ownership of the server in the tenant, and current server-bound standing authority for delegated native MCP calls. These three ordinary actions require no fresh MFA or separate owner_approved assertion. Reboot and os_update require expected_impact_digest from the preview the user confirmed. Impact is compared atomically at admission and again at execution claim; changed or incomplete evidence sends no command and requires a refreshed preview and renewed confirmation with a new request key. The body is decoded strictly: exact lowercase keys, no duplicates, no unknown fields. A replay with the same Idempotency-Key returns the stored receipt before target validation. One reboot or OS update and, separately, one update plan may be active per server; a job not finished by its deadline fails with `deadline_exceeded` and frees its slot. The action is offered in `allowed_actions` only when the server agent advertises `stackkit.host-maintenance.v1`, and `reboot` only when the server also reports `host_boot_id`. Refusals are client-error-envelope/v1 documents; 409 `reason_code` is one of control_plane_host, substrate_node, protected_demo_server, service_locked, maintenance_active, node_operation_active, plan_stale, agent_capability_missing, boot_id_unknown, agent_not_connected, heartbeat_stale, inventory_revision_stale, idempotency_key_reused, impact_confirmation_required, impact_changed or impact_unavailable; 403 carries entitlement_required or maintenance_origin_authority_denied.

operations.description: Nothing is published by default: a paired server has no public route and the relay carries no traffic. The owner enables it per server with an explicit `service` name and `target_port` (the origin is always the Guard host's loopback, never another machine) and may withdraw it at any time. The relay authenticates the Guard, not the visitor, so what answers on that port must protect itself. Enabling requires the owner, the `techstack.servers.maintenance` entitlement and a fresh multi-factor sign-in (reason `server_reach_step_up_required`); withdrawing is never gated. operations.summary: Repair named drifted host security controls
operations.description: Requests a bounded repair of controls the fresh host security evidence reports as drifted and automatically repairable. Requires the server's owner, the Edge-signed `techstack.servers.maintenance` entitlement and a fresh multi-factor sign-in (at most 300 seconds old). The repair travels as a typed, journaled Guard command that runs `stackkit host security repair --apply` for exactly the named controls; StackKits refuses, before changing anything, a change that would cut the management path or lock the owner out. Bounds: one repair per server at a time (409 `repair_in_progress`), a per-control cooldown (429 `repair_cooldown`), a daily attempt budget per control (429 `repair_attempts_exhausted`) and a circuit breaker after consecutive failures (429 `repair_circuit_open`); the 429 answers carry `retry_after`. A control that is compliant (409 `control_not_drifted`), under an approved exception (`control_has_exception`), manual (`control_not_repairable`), blocked on an authorized SSH key (`needs_authorized_key`) or not observed is refused. The body is decoded strictly.

operations.summary: Report kombify Guard host security and backup observations
operations.description: The Guard's posture channel. A full report carries what the Guard observed through the privileged executor's read-only StackKits operations: the `stackkit.host-security-evidence/v1` document of `stackkit host security verify` and the receipt states of `stackkit backup status`. A check-in (`check_in: true`) carries nothing and only asks whether a fresh observation was requested. The identity is the authenticated worker's; the control plane recomputes the verdict from the controls, judges time by its own clock, and records a document it cannot read (unknown schema version, unknown control or state, bad freshness window) as `evidence_rejected`, which leaves no earlier pass standing. A StackKits release without the command is reported as `unsupported` and shows as `security.state: unknown` with `reason_code: stackkit_cli_unsupported`. The answer is the directive: `verify_requested` and the routine cadence. Editions without posture answer `state: disabled`.
